src/business/services/VisitNotesService.ts: constructor(private readonly prisma: PrismaService) injects the ORM client directly.
src/business/services/VisitNotesService.ts:13-15: this.prisma.visitNote.create({ data: {...} }) writes to the database directly.

parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The two files don't handle storage the same way. SchedulingService reads and writes only through DAOs (PatientDao and AppointmentDao), then turns the rows into domain entities (Patient, Practitioner, Appointment). VisitNotesService injects PrismaService and calls the ORM directly (prisma.visitNote.create and prisma.visitNote.findMany) without going through a DAO. It also uses no domain entity: it returns a plain VisitNote interface built from ORM rows.

This bypasses the module's storage abstraction and breaks the consistent abstraction the rule asks for. Both candidate flags hold up against the source.

The source doesn't show whether a VisitNote DAO exists. Even so, the module's established boundary is DAO-mediated, and this file goes around it.

The concerns are related, since both deal with appointments, so cohesion alone would be acceptable. I found no validation rule written out in two places across the files.

violations.message: VisitNotesService calls the Prisma ORM directly (prisma.visitNote.create and findMany through the injected PrismaService). This goes around the DAO abstraction that the rest of the module (SchedulingService with PatientDao and AppointmentDao) uses for persistence, so the module's storage boundary is inconsistent.
